name: REF2033AIDDCR
title: REF20xx: low-drift dual-output voltage references, VREF and VREF / 2, in SOT-23-5
summary: A band-gap series reference with two buffered outputs: VREF and a second output, VBIAS, held at exactly half of it, both able to source or sink 20 mA. Each output is trimmed to ±0.05 % and drifts at most 8 ppm/°C from -40 °C to 125 °C, and the two track each other within 7 ppm/°C, so a single-supply ADC gets its reference and a mid-scale bias point from one part. Dropout is 10 mV typical, supply current 360 µA, and an enable pin drops it to a few microamps with the outputs high impedance. REF2033AIDDCR is the 3.3 V / 1.65 V version on a 3000-piece reel.
key_figures: ±6 ppm/°C max (-40 °C to 85 °C), ±7 ppm/°C max (-40 °C to 125 °C)
10 mV typ, 20 mV max at no load
360 µA typ, 430 µA max; 3.3 µA typ in shutdown

circuits.title: Low-side, current-sensing application
circuits.description: A bidirectional low-side current monitor feeding an ADC. The load current returns to ground through a 10 mΩ shunt; the INA213B reads the shunt voltage, runs from the reference's 3.0 V VREF output and has its reference input at the 1.5 V VBIAS output, so zero current sits at 1.5 V and ±2.5 A spans 250 mV to 2.75 V. The same VREF is the ADC's reference, and VREF and VBIAS track each other over temperature. EN is tied to the 5 V supply.
notes: Design targets: 5.0 V supply, ±2.5 A load current, 250 mV to 2.75 V output, ±25 mV largest shunt voltage.
Measured error over the full load range: ±0.0355 % uncalibrated and ±0.004 % calibrated at 25 °C; ±0.0522 % and ±0.0606 % from -40 °C to 125 °C.

circuits.title: Low-drift, low-side, bidirectional current-sensing topology
circuits.description: The current-sensing core alone: the reference powers the current-shunt amplifier from VREF and biases its output from VBIAS, and the amplifier output is G × ILOAD × RSHUNT above or below VBIAS.

circuits.title: 0.1 Hz to 10 Hz noise measurement setup
circuits.description: A battery supplies VIN and EN with 0.1 µF bypass. VREF carries 10 µF to ground and is AC-coupled through 40 mF into a 1 kΩ to ground, then amplified by a non-inverting stage with 10 kΩ feedback and 100 Ω to ground. A two-pole high-pass, four-pole low-pass 0.1 Hz to 10 Hz filter follows before the scope. VBIAS is left open.

where.VPOST: output at 25 °C after a cycle from 25 °C through -40 °C to 125 °C and back

equations.name: Tracking error (box method)
equations.expr: Tracking error = (VDIFF(MAX) − VDIFF(MIN)) / (VREF × Temperature range) × 10^6 ppm

where.VREF(MAX), VREF(MIN): highest and lowest output over the range

equations.name: Junction temperature
equations.note: TJ must stay at or below 150 °C.

equations.name: Current-sense transfer function
equations.expr: VOUT = G × (±VSHUNT) + VBIAS = G × (±ILOAD) × RSHUNT + VBIAS

equations.name: Largest shunt resistance
equations.expr: RSHUNT(max) = VSHUNT(max) / ILOAD(max) = 25 mV / 2.5 A = 10 mΩ

where.VSHUNT(max): largest allowed shunt voltage, 25 mV in the example
where.ILOAD(max): largest load current, 2.5 A in the example

operation.text: Two bipolar transistors run at unequal current densities; the difference of their base-emitter voltages, which rises with temperature, is developed across a resistor, scaled, and summed with a base-emitter voltage that falls with temperature, giving a band-gap voltage nearly flat over temperature. Two separate buffers derive VREF and VBIAS from that one band-gap voltage, their resistor ratios set so VBIAS is VREF / 2. Initial accuracy and temperature coefficient of both outputs are trimmed after molding (e-Trim), which also takes out errors from transistor mismatch and from the molding itself.

Since both outputs come from the same band-gap voltage, they move together with temperature: VREF − 2 × VBIAS changes by at most 7 ppm/°C from -40 °C to 125 °C and 6 ppm/°C from -40 °C to 85 °C, figured by the box method on the difference.
Each output is rated for ±20 mA. Both outputs limit at 50 mA into a short. Self-heating follows TJ = TA + PD × RθJA, and the junction must stay within its 150 °C rating.

EN high puts the part in active mode, its normal state. Pulling EN low shuts it down: the outputs go high impedance and supply current falls to about 5 µA. The logic thresholds are in the electrical characteristics: EN ≥ VIN − 0.7 V is on, EN ≤ 0.7 V is off.

Unequal thermal expansion of the package materials stresses the die during heating, so reflow can move both outputs. 92 parts, 23 on each of four 1.57 mm FR4 boards of 171.54 mm × 165.1 mm, went through one lead-free reflow; all shifted by under 0.01 %. Board size, thickness and material can give larger shifts, and every extra reflow adds to it; on a double-reflowed board the reference belongs in the second pass.
Measured on 32 parts soldered to ordinary boards, with no slots or special layout, kept in a 35 °C oven and read at intervals; typical drift is 25 ppm over the first 1000 hours.
Measured with the part soldered to a board: the 25 °C output before and after one excursion through -40 °C to 125 °C, in ppm of the nominal output.

Noise grows with the output voltage and with temperature. Extra filtering lowers it, provided the added output impedance does not spoil AC behaviour. Peak-to-peak noise is measured through a 0.1 Hz to 10 Hz band-pass (two-pole high-pass, four-pole low-pass) after an AC-coupled non-inverting gain stage.
The part runs with the supply only 20 mV above the output at no load; under load the needed headroom follows the dropout-against-load curve. A bypass capacitor of 0.1 µF to 10 µF goes on the supply.
The outputs are stable with any load capacitance from 0 µF to 10 µF.

Low-ESR 0.1 µF ceramic capacitors go at VIN, VREF and VBIAS; other chips get their own decoupling. A solid ground plane spreads heat and cuts EMI pickup. External parts sit close to the reference to avoid parasitic errors such as thermocouple (Seebeck) voltages. Reference and bias traces to the amplifier and ADC are kept short. Analog traces do not run alongside digital ones, and where they must cross they cross at right angles.

Heat, moisture and corrosive gases attack systems in vented enclosures, uncoated boards and parts whose exposed lead plating corrodes, a risk raised further by RoHS plating changes. REF2025AISDDCR (the S option) is plated in matte Sn and assembled with less exposed copper, which holds up better against corrosion in Battelle Class III and comparable harsh environments. REF2025 parts without the S use NiPdAu.

Example targets: 5.0 V supply, ±2.5 A load current, 250 mV to 2.75 V output, ±25 mV largest shunt voltage. Sensing on the low side keeps the amplifier's common-mode voltage near ground, independent of the bus voltage. Bidirectional current needs a difference amplifier with a reference input, biased at VBIAS so negative shunt voltages map below mid-scale: 1.5 V to 2.75 V is positive current, 250 mV to 1.5 V negative. Powering the amplifier from VREF and biasing it from VBIAS of the same reference keeps the two tracking over temperature. The shunt is a low-drift, tight-tolerance part (Y14870R01000B9W, 10 mΩ). The amplifier needs a 3 V single supply, a reference input, low offset and drift, fixed gain and an input range below ground: the INA213B has all of these, where instrumentation amplifiers lack the input swing to ground and need gain resistors, and difference amplifiers have higher bias current and unity or resistor-set gain. A two-point calibration at 25 °C removes offset and gain error.
